record.title: Boston Globe City Desk Copy — Held from Print (1918)
record.summary: An original in-world newspaper prop written for this Apache-2.0 starter; it is not source-verbatim Chaosium text.
record.authored_text:
BOSTON GLOBE — CITY DESK COPY — HELD FROM PRINT

HOUSE ON SHEAFE STREET LEAVES A RECORD OF MISFORTUNE

A dwelling known in the neighborhood as the Corbitt House has acquired a history that no agent's fresh paint can conceal. Successive tenants have departed after accidents, lingering illness, and self-inflicted death. No single public record explains the pattern, but the addresses and dates repeat with uncomfortable regularity.

The Macario family took the house early in 1918 and abandoned it within weeks, leaving no orderly notice. Neighbors disagree about what drove them out. Relatives will say only that members of the family are now receiving care in Roxbury.

The Globe has not established a criminal cause and will not print rumor as fact. The city desk is holding this feature until the property records, hospital accounts, and surviving tenants can be examined together.

root.opening_scene: Will the investigators accept Knott's commission, and where will they begin their inquiry?
root.one_liner: In 1920 Boston, a landlord hires you to investigate the infamous Corbitt House—the former tenants went mad, neighbors say it is haunted, and someone who should never have been buried lies beneath the basement. Ready to play without the scenario PDF.
root.win_condition: The investigators uncover the truth behind the phenomena at the Corbitt House, destroy Walter Corbitt's undead body in the basement confrontation (ideally reducing him to ash with his own ritual dagger), and leave the property in a state the landlord can manage again.
root.summary: An original derivative introductory investigation set in 1920s Boston. A landlord hires the investigators to clear the reputation of a house whose tenants have suffered accidents, illness, and madness. Research routes (newspaper morgue, hall of records, neighbors, previous tenants) converge on the Corbitt house, where an undead sorcerer still animates his buried corpse in the sealed basement.
root.player_safe_summary: In autumn 1920, Boston landlord Steven Knott inherits an old house no tenant will keep. A disaster drove the former tenants, the Macarios, from the house and left members of the family in an asylum; neighbors call the place the Corbitt House. Knott hires you by the day to uncover what is wrong and clear its reputation—you can begin at the newspaper, the Hall of Records, with neighbors and former tenants, or take the key and go straight to the house.
root.keeper_secret_summary: Walter Corbitt's body is buried behind a partition in the house's basement. His mind survives, preserving his identity through Mythos magic and animating the corpse. He misleads and terrorizes intruders before trying to murder them. His ritual dagger can bypass his sorcery and reduce him to ash.
root.author: Original classic scenario structure: Sandy Petersen / Chaosium. Narrative pack adaptation: chatrpgv4 contributors (original derivative prose; does not reproduce Chaosium Product Identity text).
root.attribution: Scenario structure inspired by the classic Call of Cthulhu introductory investigation 'The Haunting'. Scene names, NPC dialogue, and narrative prose in this pack are an original derivative work by the chatrpgv4 contributors. Numeric creature data for Walter Corbitt is referenced from rules-json/monsters.json.

This starter pack does not reproduce Chaosium Product Identity (plots, dialogue, maps, or boxed read-aloud text from the Keeper Rulebook).

record.name: Arty Wilmot
record.agenda: Guard access to the Globe clippings morgue and enjoy the little power of saying no.
record.fear: Looking weak in front of the newsroom if he caves too easily.
record.secret: He is not professionally skilled at social resistance — Regular difficulty social skills can move him; he just starts unhelpful by policy.
record.voice: Pompous, clipped, editorial. Loves denying 'the general public'.
record.keeper_note: Use Charm / Intimidate / Persuade / Fast Talk as appropriate to the approach. Pushed failures escalate (backup muscle, offence, ejection).

nodes.name: Mr. Dooley
nodes.summary: Mr. Dooley

record.name: Mr. Dooley
record.agenda: Sell papers and cigars, gossip for sport, and size people up before sharing.
record.fear: Wasting breath on snobs who look down on street vendors.
record.secret: He exaggerates; not every line is true. He can still point to the chapel ruins and name the house 'the Corbitt House'.
record.voice: Salesman banter, neighborhood Irish-Boston color, enjoys a listener.

lie_option.player_safe_line: Maybe the eyes burned bright enough to light the whole street—who can say?

deflect_options.player_safe_line: Buy a paper first, then perhaps my memory improves.

record.keeper_note: Reaction via APP/Credit Rating; failed reaction allows Charm/Fast Talk/Persuade/Intimidate from another investigator.

nodes.summary: Gabriela Macario

record.name: Gabriela Macario
record.agenda: Survive the interview without reliving every night; warn others that something evil lives in that house.
record.fear: The presence returning; questions that drag her back into the bedrooms.
record.secret: She can describe night visits and poltergeist anger but cannot give tactical specifics or Corbitt's name.
record.voice: Fragile, soft, cuts off when pressed. Speaks of 'it', not a man with a biography.

deflect_options.player_safe_line: Please—not all of it at once.

record.keeper_note: End the interview quickly when she becomes upset. Boys are with relatives in Baltimore.

record.agenda: Control access to the court file and decide whether a claimed legal contact deserves cooperation.

record.name: Steven Knott
record.agenda: Clear the Corbitt House's reputation so he can rent or sell the inherited property and stop losing money.
record.fear: Being stuck with a worthless haunted white elephant that ruins his credit.
record.secret: He knows only rumor and the Macario tragedy — nothing of Corbitt's undead nature — and will not believe Mythos explanations without hard proof.
record.voice: Practical, impatient, money-minded. Speaks in short offers and deadlines.

record.name: Vittorio Macario
record.agenda: Clutch the bible and point at the false quotation — he cannot otherwise communicate usefully.
record.fear: The burning-eyed form; being left without the book.
record.secret: His pointed line 'By his own weapon is the devil worsted!' is the dagger hint — do not overplay it.
record.voice: Mostly silent. Sudden finger on a page. Occasional babble.
record.keeper_note: Quite mad. One useful clue only. Nothing more can be gleaned.

nodes.name: Walter Corbitt
nodes.summary: Walter Corbitt

record.name: Walter Corbitt
record.agenda: Mislead and frighten intruders away from his buried body; failing that, murder them and resume feeding on residents.
record.fear: His own ritual dagger in an enemy's hand; prolonged daylight exposure of his lair; being reduced below the point where Flesh Ward and Dominate can buy rounds.
record.secret: He is an undead sorcerer animating his own corpse in the sealed basement; presentation data lives under monsters.json 'Walter Corbitt'.
record.voice: Rarely speaks. Acts through knocks, blood, flying furniture, floating knife, and finally claws.
record.keeper_note: Threat front primary danger. Uses Dominate / Flesh Ward / floating knife per the-haunting.json. Own dagger bypasses spells and turns him to ash. See monsters.json presentation sensory_signature.

source_refs.grep_anchor: Using a Fighting Maneuver to Grab the Knife

provenance.basis: Stat block, skills, spells, armor rule and Sanity loss are printed verbatim on page 459 (Walter Corbitt, Undead Fiend). The floating dagger's damage and impale line are printed on page 456. Printed armor rule (p.459): "Each point of armor reduces the damage received by 1 point. Corbitt has cast Flesh Ward already: roll 2D6 for his armor. Reduce his armor by one point for each point of damage he suffers." — the per-damage degradation is the armor_rule enum; the 2D6 initial value is rolled by the flesh-ward preparation.

weapons.name: Clawed fingernails (kick, punch, claw)
weapons.note: Page 459: Fighting 50% (Hard 25%/Extreme 10%), damage 1D3 + damage bonus (1D4) + possible infection.

weapons.name: Floating magical dagger
weapons.note: Page 456: resolved as 1D100 against Corbitt's POW opposed by the investigator's Dodge; 1D4+2 damage, 6+1D4+2 on an Extreme success (impale). Costs 1 Magic point per round and counts as Corbitt's action for that round.

attacks.name: Fighting attacks
attacks.printed: Fighting 50% (Hard 25%/Extreme 10%), damage 1D3 + damage bonus (1D4) + possible infection.
attacks.rider: On a successful attack the investigator makes a Luck roll. On failure, a day later the victim is delirious and must make a CON roll: failure = delirium 1D10 days and lose 1D10 CON; success = delirium 1D6 days, no further CON loss. Repeat until recovery or death. CON lost does not regenerate.

attacks.name: Floating knife
attacks.printed: Roll 1D100 against Corbitt's POW, opposed by the investigator's Dodge; compare levels of success. Regular or Hard success beating the Dodge inflicts 1D4+2. Extreme success impales for 6+1D4+2. Seeing the knife attack costs SAN 1/1D4.
attacks.cost: 1 Magic point per round; that point covers all actions made with the knife during the round.

profile.san_loss_to_see: 1/1D8 Sanity points to see him move

record.title: End the Corbitt Threat
record.player_safe_summary: Identify and end the malicious presence in the house—whether with its own ritual dagger, a cleansing rite, or another effective means—and bring the place lasting peace.
record.brief: Keeper-only: The scenario's mainline goal, arising once the haunting is confirmed rather than from any NPC's mouth. Corbitt animates his own corpse from the sealed basement; his own ritual dagger bypasses Flesh Ward and reduces him to ash (Vittorio's bible line hints at it). Ends only by KP semantic closure: dagger-to-ash, an equivalent sanctioned destruction, or banishment the KP accepts as final. Purely narrative completion — no machine condition can witness a destruction.

completion.narrative: Corbitt is destroyed or permanently ended by his own dagger or an equivalent KP-sanctioned means (reduced to ash, laid to rest, or banished beyond return); the house's threat is over.

failure.narrative: The investigators are wiped out, permanently retreat, or walk away with the haunting unresolved and Corbitt still feeding on the house's residents.

record.title: The Corbitt House Commission
record.player_safe_summary: Mr. Knott offers a daily fee for investigating the tenants' disappearance and the strange disturbances in the house, then asks for a written report.
record.brief: Keeper-only: Knott pays $20/day plus keys and address, and wants a report that lets him rent or sell the inherited house. He knows only rumor and the Macario tragedy — nothing of Corbitt's undead nature — and will not believe Mythos explanations without hard proof. He pressures the investigators if research exceeds a day. The report's content is the KP's call: a whitewash he can accept, or hard proof that forces him to face the truth. Finding Corbitt's remains in the basement is the decisive evidence any credible report needs.

completion.narrative: The investigators deliver a report Knott accepts (a clean bill for the house, or hard proof he cannot dodge); the KP semantically confirms the commission is discharged.

failure.narrative: Knott withdraws the commission or hires someone cheaper, or the investigation is abandoned with nothing to show for it.

record.title: Recover the Chapel Records
record.player_safe_summary: Visit the ruined chapel and recover records left by the Chapel of Contemplation; they are said to contain writings connected to Corbitt.
record.brief: Keeper-only: An optional research side path. The Chapel of Contemplation was broken up by a police raid and burned in 1912; its ruins still hold Father Thomas's journal-style records showing Corbitt's body was buried in the house basement per his will. Dooley or the court file can point investigators at the ruins. The journal materially shortcuts the basement search, so it recycles into the mainline even though the visit itself is optional.

A rust-caked knife may float and strike if they dig too close

affordances.cue: Carefully descend the neglected basement stairs (DEX/Climb).

Tear away the boards fixed to the wall and enter the foul-smelling void and the hidden chamber beyond.

affordances.cue: Spend half a day using Library Use to trace the earliest surviving construction and transfer records by the house's address.

Spend another half day researching Walter Corbitt's obituary and the lawsuit prompted by his will.
Spend another half day tracing the outcome of the second lawsuit to prevent Corbitt's burial in his own basement.

record.dramatic_question: What survived beneath the burned Chapel of Contemplation, and why does Corbitt's name appear there?
pressure_moves: Fresh white three-Y eye symbols make nearby foreheads prickle until investigators step away
Weak floorboards call for Luck, then Jump on failure; a ten-foot fall deals 1D6 damage

affordances.cue: Examine the freshly painted white triple-Y and central staring eye on the surviving wall, noting the prickling pain in your forehead as you approach.

Search the rotting cabinet and inspect beneath it; without an explicit look under the cabinet, Spot Hidden is required, and a thorough search may be pushed.

affordances.cue: Search the basement clipping room by street address for stories about the Corbitt House.
Befriend archivist Ruth Blake or explain your purpose, then ask how far back the clipping room extends and where its older records are missing.
